Curb Your Attention.work: At a 4-way intersection, a vehicle can go straight (0.55), turn left (0.30), or right (0.15). The move: mask attention to only causal agents via Amasked = A ⊙ (1 − Mfuture), preventing information leak from agents that appear only after the query agent's decision. Why it holds: an agent cannot be influenced by entities it cannot observe; gating attention to causal histories improves tail probabilities by removing non-physical coupling.

For Scaling-Aware Data Selection for E2E Driving, the concrete move is this: selects high-utility samples balancing scale and quality. In everyday terms, the paper changes raw driving evidence into a form where the car can compare choices before it moves.

Why the math helps: The math is information tradeoff. Compression is useful only when it removes redundancy while keeping the variables that change the action.
Scaling-Aware Data Selection for E2E Dri.work: A naive E2E driving model trained on all 1,000,000 collected demos is 850 MB on-disk and requires 160 ms per inference on the embedded car computer, blowing the 100 ms deadline. Data selection randomly drops 80% of training samples, shrinking the model to 170 MB, but inference drops only to 145 ms because the saved demos were not on the critical path. Scaling-aware selection picks which 20% of demos to keep by measuring how much each one improves the loss curve across multiple model sizes. The selected 200,000 demos train models that scale optimally: at 170 MB the model achieves 91% success rate (vs. 86% random), and at 100 MB it still hits 88% success—a +5 point gain at scale from intelligent data retention.
Scaling-Aware Data Selection for E2E Dri.math: The object is a utility function U(x, θ) that scores training samples by their contribution to end-to-end driving accuracy. The move: select samples by x* = arg max U(x, θ) = α task_relevance(x) + β diversity(x), balancing per-sample importance with dataset-level coverage to avoid redundancy as scale increases. Why it holds: naive scaling adds samples uniformly, but many are redundant; a Pareto-optimal selection along task relevance and diversity ensures that each added sample teaches the model something new, leading to faster convergence and better data-sample efficiency.
